summary: Eisenkot holds President Herzog's mandate until Dec 6 (extendable by up to 14 days) and has deals in principle with Yisrael Beiteinu and the Democrats. Kan and Ynet reported Thursday night that UTJ's senior rabbis approved official coalition talks with Eisenkot, but commentator Amit Segal and News.co.il say no formal approval has yet been given, with a meeting being arranged for Sunday. Bennett postponed his meeting with Eisenkot to Sunday and is still pushing for a unity government with Eisenkot serving first, while Liberman says a change government is taking shape. Shas is still reported to be staying with Netanyahu, and senior Likud officials say unity prospects are fading.

phase.now: Eisenkot has the mandate (deadline Dec 6, 2026, extendable by up to 14 days)
phase.next: UTJ is expected to meet Sunday amid conflicting reports on whether its rabbis formally approved talks with Eisenkot, and the Bennett meeting is also set for Sunday; Walla reports Eisenkot wants a government with UTJ and outside Ra'am support as early as next Wednesday. If Eisenkot fails, Herzog can task another MK for 28 days with no extension.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he wants Shas, Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism in any future government and that the public does not want one dependent on Ra'am and the Joint List. Without a majority, he needs defectors or a new partner from the other side. On Nov 5 UTJ declined to recommend any candidate, leaving Netanyahu without its endorsements, while Otzma Yehudit recommended him. Likud's delegation, last to meet Herzog, urged him to give Netanyahu the mandate, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 7 Herzog chose Eisenkot rather than Netanyahu to try first to form a government, Al Jazeera reports. Channel 12 reports Netanyahu tried to reach senior UTJ rabbis to have the party vote against an Eisenkot government, but was rebuffed, the Times of Israel reports. Ynet reports that an attempt by Netanyahu's associates to arrange a call with UTJ's Rabbi Dov Landau failed. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 13, citing an unnamed source, that Netanyahu is personally calling rabbis and sending emissaries to warn the Haredi parties off Eisenkot's bloc. On Nov 26 Haaretz reported, per the Times of Israel, that a Netanyahu representative offered seven Likud slate slots to Eisenkot-bloc members willing to defect.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu and says he won't sit with him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Championed by Yair Golan, who met Lapid and then Abbas on Oct 29; the Times of Israel says he is the only Jewish-led bloc leader openly backing a coalition with Ra'am. Without Yisrael Beiteinu it falls short, and analysts told JTA the public is not ready for it. Channel 12 reports Abbas himself privately called an Eisenkot minority government with outside Arab support weak or impossible. AFP reports Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition relying on Arab parties, and the Joint List's Jabareen says he would back him from outside. A senior Joint List official told Walla on Nov 1 that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot to the president. Ynet reports Joint List and Ra'am leaders met in Nazareth on Nov 2 and will coordinate their recommendations. Ynet reports Bennett sides with Liberman against a government relying on Arab parties, believing it would collapse. On Nov 3 Golan met Joint List leaders and they agreed to keep coordinating, while the Times of Israel notes the bloc's joint statement gave no indication of how it would govern without Arab parties. On Nov 4 Ra'am announced it will recommend Eisenkot, while Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog a government cannot be formed with Arab parties. On Nov 5 the Joint List said it will recommend Eisenkot but will not formally join his coalition, offering possible outside support, Al Jazeera and ANI report. A Times of Israel analysis notes the Joint List has not said it will back an Eisenkot-led government. Eisenkot formally received the mandate on Nov 8, and the Jerusalem Post notes the Arab parties' recommendations do not commit them to joining his coalition. On Nov 8 Liberman reiterated he will not support a government dependent on Arab parties, Ynet reports. At the Nov 10 session, Ben-Gvir and other MKs heckled the Eisenkot bloc over Arab lawmakers' absence during the anthem, and Liberman posted asking whether these were the people the bloc wanted to govern with, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 11 the bloc and the Arab MKs jointly voted to elect Yashar!'s Folkman as Arrangements Committee chair, and the Joint List accused Netanyahu's Knesset speech of racism, the Jerusalem Post reports. Middle East Monitor reports Golan said on Nov 11 that a government could be formed within three weeks with Ra'am and Joint List support. On Nov 11 the Arrangements Committee voted 13–9 to recommend Liberman as chair of the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 13 Joint List leader Jabareen listed demands for cooperating with Eisenkot's bloc, including repealing the Kaminitz Law and Arab-community crime and economic plans, which the Jerusalem Post describes as hinting at informal negotiations. On Nov 15 Golan rejected talks with Netanyahu and Likud and urged the bloc to meet Arab party leaders, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 16 Smotrich offered right-bloc support for Kahana as speaker if no deputy speakers come from Ra'am or the Joint List, and Kahana rejected the demand, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 17 Kahana was elected speaker 66–52 with the bloc's four parties plus Ra'am and the Joint List, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 22 Golan posted that a minority government is the only realistic alternative, JFeed reports. On Nov 24 the Democrats suspended talks with Yashar!, citing deadlock on a change government; Reuters notes Golan prefers a government with Arab parties and without Netanyahu. On Nov 26 the Democrats rejoined Eisenkot's bloc through a preliminary coalition deal with Yashar!, Reuters reports.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am, the Joint List and any minority government.
Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.
Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders if there are legal grounds over alleged Qatari funding.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.
JFeed reports Liberman told bloc members his party will vote against a minority government.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Ynet reports, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot authorized examining a minority government with Ra'am inside and UTJ abstaining, possibly as leverage in unity talks; Yashar says such reports are not issued on its behalf. It falls short of 61 and Liberman rejects any government dependent on Arab or Haredi parties. Unnamed sources tell Ynet that Liberman berated Eisenkot at a Saturday meeting, saying the minority-government push hurt the bloc. On Nov 8 ANI, citing Haaretz and an unnamed senior Ra'am member, reported that Ra'am will support an Eisenkot government. A senior bloc figure told Ynet on Nov 8 that Liberman has no intention of backing a narrower emergency government without a majority. Eisenkot formally received the mandate on Nov 8 with 28 days to form a government, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 8 Liberman posted that he would not help establish a government dependent on Arab parties, Ynet reports. A Ynet analysis on Nov 8, citing people close to Eisenkot, says he sees unity with Netanyahu as a last resort and may bring a minority government to a confidence vote without full coalition agreement. On Nov 8 Golan said that if Liberman wants a government that won't draft the Haredim he can form one with Netanyahu, while Liberman called Golan's criticism stupid and malicious, Ynet reports. Ynet reports that at their Nov 9 meeting Liberman asked Eisenkot to drop the idea of a minority government backed by Arab parties. On Nov 10 Ynet reported, citing unnamed sources, that Abbas has agreed in principle to Eisenkot's condition of recognizing Hamas as a terrorist organization, and Golan confirmed talks with Ra'am are underway. On Nov 17 Ra'am's Abbas warned that a minority government without the Haredi parties would be very dangerous and could not survive, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 19 the Times of Israel, citing Hebrew media and Haaretz, reported Eisenkot plans a Knesset vote on a minority government with Ra'am voting in favor without a deal and the Joint List abstaining; no statement from Eisenkot accompanied the reports. Later on Nov 19 Channel 13 reported that Bennett told Eisenkot he would not back such a government at this stage, and the Times of Israel says Liberman would vote against it. On Nov 20 Yashar officials told the Jerusalem Post the party will put a minority government to a vote before Dec 6 if talks fail, with Ra'am and the Joint List offering outside support but no ministers. Later on Nov 20 Eisenkot himself said he would form an emergency government if a broad coalition can't be built, the Times of Israel reports. Netanyahu warned on Nov 20 that such a government relying on Arab-party votes could form as early as next week and called it inconceivable, Israel National News reports. Shas's newspaper Haderech called Eisenkot's minority-government plan dangerous on its Nov 21 front page, Ynet reports. On Nov 23 Kan reported, per the Times of Israel as relayed by ANI, that Eisenkot is weighing a surprise coalition announcement and a Knesset vote within a day or two to curb defections. On Nov 24 Ynet reported that Bennett wants more time and is expected to vote against a rushed minority government, deciding only near the end of the mandate. On Nov 25 Liberman told Kan he would allow a government backed by UTJ and possibly Ra'am, Ynet reports. On Nov 26 Walla reported, per the Jerusalem Post, that Eisenkot has resolved to swear in a government even if talks with Likud and the Haredi parties fail. On Nov 26 Abbas predicted a government of the change bloc, Ra'am and UTJ with Joint List outside support, the Times of Israel reports, and Walla reports Eisenkot wants such a government with outside Ra'am support as early as next Wednesday.

blockers.text: Liberman told Ynet that supporting a minority government would hand Netanyahu the premiership.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.
Channel 13 reports Bennett told Eisenkot he won't back an Arab-backed minority government at this stage.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it. A source close to Eisenkot tells Ynet he is trying to bring Shas and UTJ into a government he leads, naming Liberman as the main obstacle. A senior UTJ official told Ynet the party would offer Eisenkot the premiership for draft exemptions, which clashes with his national-service condition; Shas is reported to be out. Unnamed senior UTJ figures say the party might back an Eisenkot government from outside without a draft law first, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 2 Liberman declined to rule out cooperating with UTJ, saying the bloc will have to see what happens. Ynet reports on Nov 3 that Eisenkot is focusing on courting the Haredi parties and that Liberman has left the door open to talks on including them. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 3 that Shas and UTJ stress no decision has been made, with their rabbis due back around the start of consultations. On Nov 4 Shas recommended Netanyahu, and Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog it would not compromise key priorities to bring Haredi parties in, Ynet reports. On Nov 5 UTJ declined to recommend either candidate, with Goldknopf telling Herzog the party is not bound to any bloc, Ynet reports. ANI reports UTJ told Herzog its support for any government depends on legislation exempting yeshiva students from service. On Nov 5 Together told Herzog it will not accept a draft-evasion law, Israel National News reports. Channel 12 reports Liberman has dropped his refusal to sit with UTJ and that the opposition is in talks with it, but Yisrael Beiteinu told the Jerusalem Post it was not aware of this. Channel 12 reports the bloc is examining a coalition with UTJ and Shas, with draft talks starting from Liberman's 2018 bill, while Shas still stands with Likud. On Nov 6 Liberman said he is willing to be flexible and compromise on the Haredi draft law, the Jerusalem Post reports. The Times of Israel reports Liberman has confirmed he is open to a coalition with Haredi parties, reversing a key promise. After Liberman's shift, Eisenkot reiterated his demand for mandatory national service, the Times of Israel reports, and UTJ said it will back whoever solves the draft issue, Israel National News reports. UTJ leader Asher said on Nov 6 that no coalition proposal has yet been made to the party and that its rabbis will decide on any offer, the Times of Israel reports. Al Jazeera notes that adding UTJ and Shas would give Eisenkot a bare majority, as Herzog prepares to hand him the mandate. On Nov 7 Golan said he is open to a government with the Haredim on conditions including enlistment of young Haredim and no blank check, adding that they must come to meet his party in Ramat Gan. An unnamed Shas Council of Torah Sages source told Channel 12 that Shas would not act against UTJ's rabbis if they approve a deal, but Shas itself called reports it could join an Eisenkot government fake news, the Times of Israel reports. Ynet reports on Nov 8 that Likud's main pressure is on Deri, whom Likud officials expect, though not with certainty, to refuse the opposition; a senior bloc figure told Ynet the only option is the bloc plus the Haredi parties, or another election. Eisenkot formally received the mandate on Nov 8 with 28 days to form a government, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 8 Liberman said he still backs military service for Haredi men while seeking understandings with the Haredi parties, Ynet reports. On Nov 9 the Jerusalem Post, citing unnamed UTJ sources, reports no agreement yet on joining Eisenkot, with conditions on Shabbat, kashrut, conversion and the religious status quo, and assessments that Shas would follow if UTJ joins first. Kikar HaShabbat reporter Yishai Cohen told 103FM that Shas could consider backing Eisenkot if yeshiva students' status is settled, but is waiting for UTJ to move first. On Nov 9 Ynet reported that Yashar invited Shas and UTJ to back a bid to replace Speaker Ohana at the Knesset's opening session; UTJ declined and Shas was not expected to join, while UTJ has not denied talks with the change bloc. On Nov 9 Kan reported that Eisenkot and Liberman agreed to open talks with Shas and UTJ, offering a softened draft law with a transition period, and Channel 12 said the talks were at an early stage, the Times of Israel reports. An unnamed senior UTJ source told JFeed a significant week lies ahead on cooperation with the change bloc, conditional on preserving the religious status quo. On Nov 10 Ynet reported, citing unnamed sources, that the bloc's parties intend first to try a government with the Haredi parties, and that Liberman has told Eisenkot he will bring them in. On Nov 10 UTJ leader Asher told Kikar HaShabbat the party won't join any coalition without draft exemptions, untouched Haredi school funding and the religion-state status quo, and Goldknopf told Channel 12 there have been preliminary contacts with Eisenkot's camp, the Times of Israel reports. The same day Shas said it still supports Netanyahu and is not in talks with any other player, the Times of Israel reports. Ynet reports Netanyahu met Asher on Nov 9 to keep UTJ from joining Eisenkot, and Asher gave no commitment. HNGN reports Asher said UTJ will not back replacing Speaker Ohana before a new government is formed. On Nov 11 the Jerusalem Post reported internal divisions within Eisenkot's bloc amid the Haredi coalition talks. A Jerusalem Post analysis on Nov 11 says Eisenkot chose Kahana over Lapid for Speaker, citing unnamed sources, and that the pick could strain ties with the Haredi parties. On Nov 12 the Times of Israel cited Channel 12 reporting that Rabbi Moshe Hillel Hirsch authorized UTJ to open talks with Eisenkot's bloc and that Asher met Liberman on Nov 11, with both sides saying no formal negotiations are underway; Hirsch himself said he doubts a deal is realistic, and Kan reports Moshe Gafni is working to block one. On Nov 12 Kan reported that senior UTJ figures have opened a regular channel with Ra'am and Joint List leaders to share updates on their talks with Eisenkot's bloc, while Asher's office called his conversations with Abbas and Tibi casual, JFeed reports. On Nov 12 Ynet reported, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot's bloc is weighing a one-year suspension of draft enforcement, including arrests, to win UTJ's support. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 13 that Eisenkot's camp wants UTJ in first with Ra'am abstaining and Shas later, that Liberman prefers Shas from the start, and that Deri has yet to decide. On Nov 13 the Times of Israel, citing Channel 12, reported that Agudat Yisrael's rabbinic advisers want every MK in Eisenkot's bloc to sign a pledge on a draft-exemption law with a court override clause. Ynet reports on Nov 13, citing unnamed bloc sources, that the preferred route is UTJ joining a minority government first, then Shas or Likud defectors, and that progress has been made with the Haredi parties. HNGN reports the bloc suspects Golan and Bennett are not committed to a coalition with the Haredi parties. The Jerusalem Post reports that on Nov 11 UTJ MKs Porush and Stark filed a bill freezing draft-evasion arrests and enforcement pending a yeshiva-student law, while Bennett filed a bill cutting support to households that neither serve nor work. On Nov 14 the Times of Israel cited Channel 12 reporting that Eisenkot has decided to prioritize a coalition with the Haredi parties, and Channel 13 reporting that UTJ is debating joining without a guaranteed draft exemption, seeking instead a one-year halt to yeshiva-student enlistment and a freeze on arrests and sanctions. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 14, citing unnamed bloc sources, that there is no consensus in the bloc on including the Haredi parties and that some suspect Bennett may prefer a new election, which it notes Bennett has not said publicly. On Nov 15 Bennett urged the bloc to pressure the Haredi parties rather than plead with them, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 15 the Times of Israel reported UTJ has yet to commit on the speaker vote, with Netanyahu pressing it to oppose Kahana. On Nov 15 a senior UTJ source told Channel 12 the sides are in daily contact and making real progress, while Asher called reports of dramatic progress baseless, the Times of Israel reports. Channel 12 also reports Deri privately says a Haredi draft law cannot pass before a government is sworn in, and an unnamed Shas figure said Shas won't negotiate with Eisenkot's bloc. UTJ MK Pindrus told Meet the Press that Shas could eventually join if a yeshiva-student arrangement is reached, while Shas denied plans to join, The Media Line reports. Yedioth Ahronoth reports Eisenkot met Asher privately last week, Anadolu reports, and Haaretz reported on Nov 16 that UTJ sources cite significant progress in talks with the bloc. On Nov 17 UTJ leader Asher said the party won't back Kahana for speaker and has not decided whether its MKs will oppose or abstain, the Times of Israel reports. Later on Nov 17 i24NEWS, citing Ynet, reported that Rabbi Hirsch instructed Degel HaTorah's MKs to back Likud's Katz for speaker, with UTJ's other MKs also announcing support. UTJ ultimately voted for Likud's Katz when Kahana was elected speaker 66–52 on Nov 17, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 18 Ynet reported that Yashar! MKs presented a draft framework giving Haredi draft evaders aged 18–26 up to six months to regularize their status through one of three tracks, with sanctions for those who don't, and that UTJ sources expect the rabbis to reject it. An unnamed UTJ official told Ynet it seems easier to reach draft understandings with Liberman than with Eisenkot, while UTJ disputes reports of advanced talks. On Nov 18 JFeed, citing Kikar HaShabbat, reported unnamed Degel HaTorah officials saying draft talks are deadlocked over Eisenkot's proposed 3% quota for Torah students, which Rabbi Lando told his representative not to accept. Arutz Sheva, citing Channel 13, reports a Haredi demands document for talks with Eisenkot and Liberman seeking exemptions without quotas or sanctions, an end to arrests, an override clause and signed commitments from every bloc faction. On Nov 21 Ynet reported Eisenkot's draft framework would retroactively regularize about 90,000 Haredi men through age-based tracks with sanctions, and a UTJ official told Ynet an understanding with Liberman would be easier than with Eisenkot. On Nov 22 unnamed UTJ officials told Ynet the party will watch from the sidelines and back whichever bloc offers a better draft-exemption law, while Shas is said to remain loyal to Netanyahu's bloc. Israel National News, citing Kan, reports Liberman is now in direct contact with UTJ chairman Asher. On Nov 24 Maariv reported, per JFeed, that UTJ MKs Asher, Goldknopf, Pindrus and Porush are preparing formal talks with Eisenkot and Liberman, with Rabbi Landau's green light and Rabbi Hirsch's approval still pending, while Likud tries to halt the process. On Nov 24 Yeshiva World News, citing Channel 14, reported that Deri told Netanyahu and senior UTJ officials Shas will not join an Eisenkot-led government and warned that UTJ joining alone would deepen a rift in the Haredi bloc. On Nov 24 Channel 12 reported, per israel.com, that UTJ named Asher, Goldknopf, Pindrus and Porush as its negotiating team, with rabbinic approval still sought before formal talks begin. On Nov 24 Yashar! said Eisenkot and Liberman agreed to sign a coalition agreement, Reuters reports; JFeed reports Liberman told the bloc the only option is a government with Shas and UTJ. Asher said reports of progress with the Eisenkot bloc do not reflect reality, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 25 Liberman told Kan that UTJ MKs had their rabbis' green light and talks were progressing well, Ynet reports; JNS reports no deal yet and Haredi sources say Netanyahu is working to block one. On Nov 25 Hebrew media reported Asher was meeting Netanyahu, while UTJ's contacts with Eisenkot's bloc remain unofficial, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 25 the Jerusalem Post reported UTJ and the bloc agreed to freeze the religion-state status quo and a three-month halt on deserter arrests, and Walla reported their talks would become official. On Nov 26 the Jerusalem Post reported that legal teams for Yashar! and UTJ are drafting an agreement, with UTJ expected to get the housing ministry and the Finance Committee chair, and Walla reported about 75% of the details agreed; Shas, needed to reach a majority, is still reported to be staying out. Ynet reports Eisenkot is seeking to finalize deals with Bennett and Golan by Saturday night, with UTJ talks on a draft framework running on a separate track. On Nov 26 Kikar HaShabbat reported that Eisenkot accepted UTJ's veto on Democrats MK Kariv, a Reform rabbi, as education minister, while UTJ denies negotiating posts, the Times of Israel reports. Goldknopf said the same day that Liberman apologized to him for past remarks about Haredim, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 26 Kan reported Yashar! and UTJ reached agreement on key principles of a Haredi draft law in unofficial talks, and Ynet reported UTJ's senior rabbis then approved opening official coalition talks with Eisenkot, the Times of Israel reports. Late on Nov 26 Amit Segal and News.co.il reported that the rabbis had not yet given official approval and that a Sunday meeting is being arranged, Israel.com reports.

blockers.text: Channel 14 reports Deri told Netanyahu and UTJ officials Shas won't join an Eisenkot-led government.
On Nov 10 Shas said it still supports Netanyahu and is not negotiating with any other player.
UTJ's Asher says the party won't join any coalition that doesn't meet its draft, school-funding and status-quo demands.
Shas called reports it could join an Eisenkot government fake news and said it is part of the right-wing bloc.
Haredi sources tell the Jerusalem Post that Deri won't join an opposition-led government without Likud.
Shas and UTJ say they won't join any government unless yeshiva students' exemptions are written into law.
Liberman long pledged not to sit with Shas and UTJ, but on Nov 6 said he would compromise on the draft law.
Eisenkot's core promise is national service for all.
Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog it rejects compromising security and economic priorities to include Haredi parties.
Together told Herzog it will not accept a law exempting Haredim from the draft.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu-linked sources are promoting it, possibly with a rotating premiership and without Shas and UTJ. Kan cites Netanyahu associate Benny Biton as saying Netanyahu wants unity, and an unnamed Likud official named Herzog and Trump as guarantors for Eisenkot. Channel 12 reports Liberman wants Eisenkot to join Netanyahu, though not under his own banner. Who would lead it is the sticking point. Likud whip Ofir Katz told Army Radio the party opposes rotation and others can join the existing coalition. Channel 14 reports, citing unnamed sources, that Netanyahu has given up on unity talks and is preparing for a new election. Ynet reports Netanyahu told associates privately he is not ruling out any option, including rotation, and that Katz says unity is off if the opposition ousts Speaker Ohana. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he is open to a broad government with any party that does not support terrorism but that he should lead it; an associate told Ynet no unity proposal has yet been made. Israel Hayom reports a Likud source's assessment, not a negotiated offer, that Netanyahu could accept unity if he served about two years and then became president, with Eisenkot taking over. ANI, citing the Times of Israel, reports Shas Council of Torah Sages member Rabbi Moshe Maya urged a unity government. On Nov 5 Yashar's delegation rejected a unity government with Netanyahu and called him the obstacle to unity, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 5 Likud MK Yoav Kisch urged a broad national government and called on the opposition to end its boycott, the Times of Israel reports. After Herzog's decision on Nov 7, Netanyahu called in a video for a national unity government including all his current allies, which the Times of Israel calls a likely non-starter. Kan reports, citing an unnamed associate, that Netanyahu would discuss rotation if unity talks were held, and that an envoy's approach to Eisenkot was rebuffed; Yashar said it knew of no such approach and that Likud can join an Eisenkot-led coalition without extremists. Ynet reports on Nov 8 that Netanyahu is expected to pursue unity in the coming days, though unnamed senior Likud ministers had privately called it too costly and preferred another election; Yashar called his speech hysterical and said it would consider unity only if Likud breaks with its extremists. On receiving the mandate on Nov 8, Eisenkot appealed to Likud and Smotrich's party to join a government he would lead, AFP reports. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 9 that Netanyahu has launched an effort to block an Eisenkot government while still calling for unity, with disputes over who would lead it. In his Nov 10 Knesset speech Netanyahu again asked MKs to form a national unity government, and Eisenkot replied that the speech was hate-filled and Netanyahu unfit for office, urging a national emergency government instead, the Jerusalem Post reports. Yashar had announced a preliminary negotiating meeting with Likud for Nov 11, but Eisenkot cancelled it after Netanyahu's Nov 10 speech, while Likud said it would meet any faction seeking unity, the Jerusalem Post reports. Ynet reports on Nov 10 that the planned Likud–Yashar! meeting is cancelled, Likud has not formally set up a negotiating team, and contacts between Eisenkot envoy Ronen Manelis and Netanyahu's lawyer Michael Rabello are moving away from a deal. In his Nov 10 speech Netanyahu ruled out rotation and said a unity government must include all national-camp parties, including the Haredim, Ynet reports. Haaretz reports on Nov 11 that leaders of Eisenkot's bloc learned of the planned Yashar!–Likud talks only after they were cancelled. On Nov 11 Smotrich urged Netanyahu and Eisenkot to sit together and said understandings can be reached, Ynet reports. Ynet reported late on Nov 11, citing sources close to Netanyahu, that Likud would not insist on including Otzma Yehudit in a unity government; Likud denied it, saying Netanyahu called for unity based on the right-wing bloc's parties. Ynet reports on Nov 13, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot has told his team to resume talks with Likud next week, with unity seen as an option if Haredi talks stall. Channel 12 reports, per the Times of Israel on Nov 14, that Yashar! plans to keep the door open to Likud and Religious Zionism, but not Otzma Yehudit, and to meet Likud next week. On Nov 14 Netanyahu urged talks without preconditions, and Eisenkot replied that Likud must accept his principles and his leadership, with Likud and Yashar! teams set to meet Sunday, Nov 15, Ynet and the Times of Israel report. On Nov 15 Yashar! named Horowitz and Tropper as negotiators and invited Likud to include MK Elisha Madan, who backs unity, JFeed reports, while Ynet says the teams remain divided over who would lead. On Nov 15 Religious Zionism's Strock called for a unity government and warned against relying on Arab parties, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 15 Likud and Yashar! negotiators met for about an hour in Herzliya, with a Bennett envoy present, and said in a joint statement the dialogue will continue, JFeed reports. Yashar! denied a report that it offered a rotation and said its only proposal is for Likud to join an Eisenkot-led government, the Times of Israel reports. Hebrew media report the Nov 15 meeting made no progress; Channel 12 says Likud asked Yashar! to hold off on Kahana as speaker and was refused, and that Tropper said Eisenkot is determined to form a government in any scenario, the Times of Israel reports. Channel 13 reports Liberman opposed the meeting as a trap, and Channel 12 reports Bennett wants Eisenkot to go first in any rotation and won't join Likud without his bloc partners. Israel Hayom reports, citing unnamed figures, that Netanyahu's associates told Eisenkot Likud would not insist on including Otzma Yehudit, though Netanyahu publicly insists on all his allies, the Times of Israel notes. The Jerusalem Post reports Eisenkot plans to hold talks with Religious Zionism but not Otzma Yehudit. Hours after the Nov 15 meeting, Eisenkot said Netanyahu cannot remain prime minister and demanded an investigation into a Channel 12 report on election-eve arrests of Ra'am members, and Likud called his statement incitement, Al Jazeera reports. On Nov 16 Yisrael Beiteinu MK Malinovsky reaffirmed in a radio interview that the party won't join a Netanyahu-led unity government, the Jerusalem Post reports. At Nov 16 faction meetings Golan and Liberman both rejected a unity government with Netanyahu, with Golan citing Gantz's experience, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 17 an unnamed senior Eisenkot-bloc official told Kan there is no chance of a unity government, citing Netanyahu's stolen-election claims and the Mossad chief's US trip, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 17 Netanyahu again called for a unity government including all parties and the Haredim, said he would not rest a government on Ra'am, and left without answering a question on rotation, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 18 Netanyahu met Bennett at the Knesset for a security briefing, Likud said, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 18 Bennett met Netanyahu for about two and a half hours without informing Eisenkot, and an unnamed Bennett associate told Ynet he is working for a unity government headed by Eisenkot. Unnamed Eisenkot-bloc sources told Ynet that Likud had sought a full term for Netanyahu with no rotation and a guaranteed place for Ben-Gvir, which a Likud source disputed, saying rotation had not been raised. After the Nov 18 meeting, Bennett told bloc leaders a unity government was needed and a rotation with Eisenkot first was possible, while Liberman and Golan said they would not sit with Netanyahu in any form, JFeed reports citing Channel 13. The bloc's five leaders then jointly called for a national emergency government headed by Eisenkot, Ynet reports, and Likud's Karhi told Kan that Eisenkot is not Likud's only potential partner in the other bloc, the Times of Israel reports. Members of Bennett's entourage told the Jerusalem Post on Nov 18 that he won't join a unity government under Netanyahu and that the only scenario relevant to him is a rotation with Eisenkot serving first. An unnamed Likud source told Maariv on Nov 18 that Netanyahu serving second in a rotation with Eisenkot cannot be ruled out, though the source said Netanyahu's position remains that he should lead, the Jerusalem Post reports. Ynet reports on Nov 18, citing Eisenkot-bloc sources, that Likud's negotiators set five conditions: a full term for Netanyahu, the Bismuth draft framework, no state commission on Oct. 7, Ben-Gvir's inclusion and no repeal of judicial-overhaul laws; a Likud source said the first meeting was preliminary and those issues were not discussed in detail. On Nov 19 Likud said it keeps extending its hand for national unity and that the negotiating teams will meet again on Sunday, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 20 Netanyahu said he had briefed Liberman, Bennett and Eisenkot on security in recent days and urged them to work toward a unity government, Israel National News reports. On Nov 21 Ynet, citing Eisenkot-bloc sources, reported Likud's demands as Netanyahu staying PM for the full term without rotation, no state commission on Oct 7 and Ben-Gvir in government; a Likud official disputed parts of this, and unnamed figures floated Netanyahu moving to the presidency after two years. On Nov 21 the Times of Israel reported Yashar! invited Likud to 'marathon' talks on Sunday, with Likud seeking an end to boycotts of Netanyahu and a renunciation of 'terror supporting' parties. AFP reports Likud's unity guidelines also include keeping Israel's security zones in Syria, Lebanon and Gaza and rejecting Palestinian statehood, and that Yashar! says the talks are due to begin on Sunday, Nov 22. On Nov 22 the teams met for the 'marathon' talks, with Likud sending MK Ofir Katz and attorney Michael Rabello and Yashar! sending MK Chili Tropper, Yoav Horowitz and Guy Gutman, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 22 Likud's Ofir Katz opened the new round saying Likud expects real negotiations, JFeed reports. On Nov 22 the negotiating teams met for nearly four hours without a deal; JFeed, citing briefings, reports Likud refused Eisenkot's demand to exclude Ben-Gvir, the leadership question was not raised, and both sides agreed to meet again. Ynet reports on Nov 22 that rotation was not discussed, Yashar! rejected Likud's request to halt judicial legislation, Likud wanted Haredi representatives present for draft talks, and the sides agreed on a Jewish nation-state and no Palestinian state, with another meeting planned later this week. On Nov 23 Golan urged Eisenkot to halt what he called deceitful talks with Likud's team, Haaretz reports. On Nov 23 Golan warned Bennett that a unity government keeping Netanyahu in power would endanger Israel, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 23 the teams met for over two hours at the Knesset, focusing on the judicial overhaul, and agreed in a joint statement to meet again without announcing a breakthrough, Ynet reports. The Times of Israel reports, citing Walla and Channel 12, that Likud rejected Yashar!'s demand to repeal the whole judicial overhaul and its request to discuss term limits, and Channel 13 reports Eisenkot wants a deadline for the talks while Bennett prefers none. Ynet reports on Nov 24 that at Monday's round Yashar! refused Likud's request to halt its legislation, said it would advance term limits for the prime minister and sought a judicial-selection framework approved by the attorney general, while Likud said it would discuss any proposal; rotation was not raised. On Nov 24 the Democrats said Yashar! and Likud had agreed to set up a consensus committee on the judicial overhaul, Ynet reports, and the two sides are set for a fourth round on Wednesday, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 25 Liberman told Kan the Likud talks were unnecessary and lend Netanyahu legitimacy, and the Times of Israel reports significant gaps remain ahead of the fourth round. On Nov 25 the Yashar! and Likud teams met for a fourth round of unity talks, the Jerusalem Post reports, and the Democrats said in a statement that a unity government must be taken off the table. On Nov 26 senior Likud officials told Walla that unity prospects are fading, the Jerusalem Post reports, and Bennett denied a Haaretz report that his aide ran a secret unity channel with Netanyahu's representatives, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 26 the Democrats, who had suspended talks over the unity track, agreed in principle to join an Eisenkot coalition, Reuters reports. On Nov 26 Ynet reported Bennett has held direct talks with Likud's Ron Dermer; Bennett confirmed contacts with Netanyahu's camp, saying Eisenkot knows of them, the Times of Israel reports.

blockers.text: Eisenkot cancelled a planned preliminary meeting with Likud after Netanyahu's Nov 10 Knesset speech.
Likud whip Ofir Katz said the party opposes a rotation of the premiership.
Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation.
Channel 12 reports Liberman still refuses to join a Netanyahu-led government, even as he urges Eisenkot to.
Ben-Gvir warned Netanyahu against a unity government with Eisenkot.
Together MK Merav Cohen warned against a unity deal with Likud, saying "You don't make deals with scorpions."
Likud's reported unity conditions include ending 'political boycotts' of Netanyahu and formally renouncing 'terror supporting' parties.
Likud MK Miki Zohar called the talks a sham and said Netanyahu must serve first as prime minister.
The Democrats suspended coalition talks with Yashar! over its progress toward a unity government with Netanyahu.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu Plus Bennett's Together
scenarios.note: Ideologically the closest fit, but Bennett and Lapid campaigned on replacing Netanyahu.

blockers.text: Bennett declared on election night that Netanyahu has lost.

מחל.stance: On Nov 26 Likud MK Amir Ohana said the rival bloc will form a government without Likud, the Jerusalem Post reports, citing Walla.
red_lines: No government that depends on Arab parties

דרך.stance: Leaving a committee meeting on Nov 25, Eisenkot told Walla he is optimistic a government will be formed, saying "It will happen."
red_lines: Partners must accept his four principles

רק.stance: On Nov 26 Bennett confirmed talks with Netanyahu's associates, calling a unity government initially led by Eisenkot the best option and a UTJ–Arab-backed one worse, Ynet reports via the Times of Israel.
red_lines: No government reliant on Arab parties (per Ynet)

אמת.stance: On Nov 26 the Democrats and Yashar! said in a joint statement they agreed in principle to join a coalition, with the Democrats getting four ministries, Reuters reports.

ל.stance: On Nov 26 Liberman said a change government is taking shape and warned that Netanyahu would try to thwart it, the Jerusalem Post reports.

שס.stance: Channel 14 reports Deri told Netanyahu and senior UTJ officials that Shas will stay in the right-wing bloc and not join an Eisenkot-led government, per Yeshiva World News.

ג.stance: On Nov 26 UTJ's senior rabbis, Lando and Hirsch, reportedly approved launching official coalition talks with Eisenkot, Ynet reports via the Times of Israel.
red_lines: Haredi school funding not tied to core curriculum

ב.stance: On Nov 22 Ben-Gvir posted that Eisenkot's condemnation of settler violence amounted to capitulation to the Arab parties, SBS News reports.

ט.stance: Smotrich urged the opposition leaders to join Netanyahu's bloc, Ynet reports.

עם.stance: On Nov 26 Abbas told Kan's Makan radio he expects a government of the change bloc's parties, Ra'am and UTJ, with Joint List outside support, the Times of Israel reports.

ודם.stance: On Nov 16 Jabareen said the Joint List asked the attorney general to investigate Netanyahu and demanded a state commission of inquiry, the Jerusalem Post reports.

timeline.text: Saudi broadcaster Al-Hadath reports, citing an unnamed Israeli source, that the White House is arranging a Trump–Eisenkot meeting once he forms a government.
Amit Segal and News.co.il report UTJ's rabbis have not yet formally approved talks with Eisenkot, contradicting earlier Kan and Ynet reports.
Liberman said the change government is taking shape and warned Netanyahu would try to thwart it.
Ynet reports UTJ rabbis Lando and Hirsch approved official coalition talks with Eisenkot, with UTJ MKs to meet their lawyer Sunday first.
Kan reports Yashar! and UTJ reached agreement in unofficial talks on key principles of a Haredi draft law.
Walla reports Bennett postponed Thursday evening's coalition meeting with Eisenkot to Sunday, seeking a detailed framework on military service needs.
Goldknopf told Kol Hai radio that Liberman apologized for past remarks about Haredim and is working for an Eisenkot government with UTJ.
Abbas told Kan's Makan radio he expects a government of the change bloc, Ra'am and UTJ, with the Joint List as a safety net.
Bennett confirmed talks with Netanyahu's camp, reported by Ynet to involve Ron Dermer, but said his party will not move to Netanyahu's bloc.
Kikar HaShabbat reports Eisenkot agreed to UTJ's veto on Reform rabbi Gilad Kariv as education minister; UTJ denies negotiating posts.
The Democrats and Yashar! agreed in principle on a coalition deal giving Golan's party public security, labor and welfare, communications, and culture and sport, Reuters reports.
Ynet reports Bennett has stayed publicly silent and is waiting to see the Haredi concessions and Eisenkot's plans for Ra'am before declaring his position.
Maariv reports Eisenkot's bloc aims to sign and submit all coalition agreements to the Knesset by Tuesday, Dec 1, or Wednesday at the latest, the Jerusalem Post reports.
The Jerusalem Post reports Yisrael Beiteinu is expected to get defense, justice and aliyah, with Liberman as defense minister and Oded Forer the leading pick for justice.
The Jerusalem Post reports lawyers for Yashar! and UTJ are drafting a coalition agreement, while UTJ says it is not discussing ministerial posts.
Senior Likud officials told Walla unity prospects are fading, and Likud MK Ohana said the rival bloc will form a government without Likud, the Jerusalem Post reports.
Channel 12 reports Eisenkot aims to sign deals with Bennett and Golan before Shabbat, and Channel 13 says the Democrats won't get any of the four senior ministries, Israel National News reports.
Bennett denied a Haaretz report that his aide ran a secret unity channel with Netanyahu's representatives, the Times of Israel reports.
Haaretz reports a Netanyahu representative offered seven Likud slate slots to Eisenkot-bloc members willing to defect, the Times of Israel reports.
Reuters reports Eisenkot has resumed meetings with the left-wing Democrats as coalition talks gain momentum.
Kan reports Netanyahu told aides he is not optimistic Eisenkot will fail, while Likud called the report fake news, the Times of Israel reports.
Eisenkot met President Herzog on Wednesday to update him on the talks but did not tell him he had assembled a government, the Times of Israel reports.
Hebrew media report a draft portfolio split giving Liberman defense, Bennett finance and Lapid foreign affairs, with the justice ministry still disputed, per the Times of Israel.
Kan reports UTJ's rabbis could approve formal coalition talks with Eisenkot's bloc as soon as Thursday, the Times of Israel reports.
The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu asked Asher not to rush into a deal with Eisenkot's bloc, and Asher said UTJ had no other option.
The Jerusalem Post reports UTJ and Eisenkot's bloc agreed to freeze the religion-state status quo, and Walla says their talks will become official.
The Yashar! and Likud negotiating teams met on Wednesday for a fourth round of unity talks in about two weeks, the Jerusalem Post reports.
The Democrats said in a statement on Wednesday that a unity government must be taken off the table, the Jerusalem Post reports.
Eisenkot told Walla he is optimistic about forming a government despite reported portfolio disputes with the Democrats, the Times of Israel reports.
Channel 12 reports Golan wants defense, foreign affairs or finance, while Eisenkot wants to keep justice and education and offered national security, per the Times of Israel.
